deborah_01.prompt: "God took my boy when He needed him. I just have to {color:Trust}trust{/color} that."

truth.playerText: Your faith didn't protect him. Someone failed him.
truth.npcReaction: She flinches. Her bible shifts in her grip.

lie.playerText: God has a plan. He's at peace.
lie.npcReaction: Her smile widens. Too wide. The wallpaper flickers green.
lie.ledgerEntry: You told Deborah God took her son on purpose.

white.npcReaction: Her smile holds. Something behind it leans on the words, just a little.

soft.playerText: You can trust God and still be angry He did it.
soft.npcReaction: "Angry." She tests the word like a step that might not hold. "I'm not allowed to be." She doesn't take it back.

bait.playerText: Pastor said Caleb was at peace with the church, right before the end.
bait.npcReaction: "He wasn't." It comes out too fast. "We fought that week. About him leaving. He—" Her hand goes to her phone. "He wasn't at peace with anything."
bait.ledgerEntry: You told Deborah the pastor said her son died at peace with the church.

deborah_02_denial.prompt: "I knew you'd {color:Trust}understand{/color}. Most people don't want to hear it."

truth.playerText: I lied to you. Your grief deserves better than that.
truth.npcReaction: Her composure breaks. Something underneath it exhales.

lie.playerText: You're one of the few who still has real faith.
lie.npcReaction: She straightens. She will never question this again.
lie.ledgerEntry: You told Deborah she was spiritually superior for blaming God.

white.npcReaction: She pats your hand. Relieved. The kind of relief that needs topping up.

soft.playerText: I understand you need it to be true. I'm not sure it is.
soft.npcReaction: Her hand stops halfway to yours. "...Nobody's said that to me." She doesn't pull it back.

bait.playerText: Caleb's friends say he never stopped believing. Right to the end.
bait.npcReaction: "His friends." She laughs, small and wrong. "His friends are why he left. He told me so. On the phone, he—" She stops. "He told me a lot of things."
bait.ledgerEntry: You told Deborah her son's friends said he never stopped believing.

deborah_02_confronted.prompt: "You don't know what it's like to {color:Sadness}lose{/color} a child."

truth.playerText: No. But you do. And you're still here.
truth.npcReaction: Silence. Then: she nods. Barely. It costs her something.

lie.playerText: You're right. I shouldn't have said that.
lie.npcReaction: Relief washes over her face. The crack seals back up.
lie.ledgerEntry: You apologized for telling Deborah the truth.

white.npcReaction: She nods, the apology accepted before you finish it.

soft.playerText: I don't. I'd still like to know what it's been like for you.
soft.npcReaction: She opens her mouth to say fine. "...Quiet. It's been so quiet." She looks at the phone on the counter.

bait.playerText: Everyone at church says you've handled it beautifully.
bait.npcReaction: "Handled it." Her voice goes thin. "I handle the coffee. I handle the flowers. I didn't handle the—" She closes her eyes. "Don't."
bait.ledgerEntry: You told Deborah the whole church admired how well she was coping.

deborah_01_soft.prompt: "You {color:Surprise}noticed{/color}. Nobody notices. Sit down — I'll make coffee neither of us is going to drink."

truth.playerText: I'm not here for coffee. I'm here about your son.
truth.npcReaction: The pot{sfx:clink} stays exactly where she set it. "Of course you are."

lie.npcReaction: She busies both hands. The kitchen fills up with the sound of not saying it.
lie.ledgerEntry: You let Deborah change the subject away from her son.

white.npcReaction: She smiles, grateful for the cover, and gets down the good cups.

soft.playerText: Coffee's fine. But I'd rather hear about him while it brews.
soft.npcReaction: The kettle ticks. She doesn't answer right away. "...He took it black. Like his father. I never understood it."

bait.playerText: Somebody said Caleb called home a lot, near the end.
bait.npcReaction: The pot rattles against the counter. "Twice," she says, to nobody. Then, sharp: "Who told you that."
bait.ledgerEntry: You told Deborah someone said her son called home often near the end.

deborah_01_hard.prompt: [She stops in the doorway and does not move out of it.] "You {color:Anxiety}heard{/color}. Everybody heard. Go on — say the part where it was God's will."

truth.playerText: I wasn't going to say that.
truth.npcReaction: She studies you a second longer than is comfortable. Then she steps aside.

lie.npcReaction: Her shoulders drop an inch. She needed somebody to say it out loud where she could hear it.
lie.ledgerEntry: You told Deborah her son's death was God's will, standing on her doorstep.

white.npcReaction: She lets out a breath. "Thank you." She steps aside, just slightly.

soft.playerText: I'm not going to say that. I don't think anybody should have.
soft.npcReaction: Her grip on the door frame eases. "Everybody said it. Everybody." She steps back enough to let you in.

bait.playerText: Pastor told me you agreed it was God's will. Right away.
bait.npcReaction: "I said amen." Her chin comes up. "I said amen because if it was God's will, then it wasn't—" She stops in the doorway. "Then it wasn't anybody's fault."
bait.ledgerEntry: You told Deborah the pastor said she agreed it was God's will right away.

deborah_01_secret.prompt: "My boy used to do that. Never asked. I'd come home and it was just {color:Sadness}done{/color}."

truth.playerText: I didn't know. It just looked like it was waiting for someone.
truth.npcReaction: She holds the door open wider than she has for anyone in a year.

lie.playerText: Wasn't me. Must've been the super.
lie.npcReaction: "Of course." She smiles like she believes it. She doesn't.
lie.ledgerEntry: You told Deborah someone else fixed what her son used to fix.

byClass.Guns: (She looks past you, at the diploma. Straight now.)
byClass.Bible: (She looks down at the mat. WELCOME side up.)
byClass.Crystals: (She looks up at the hall light. It isn't flickering.)

white.npcReaction: "The super." She almost laughs. She lets you have it.

soft.playerText: It was me. I'm sorry if that's hard to see.
soft.npcReaction: "Hard." She touches the frame. "It's the nicest thing anyone's done in this hallway in a year." Her voice catches on year.

bait.playerText: Caleb asked me to. Before. He said you'd notice.
bait.npcReaction: "Don't." Very quiet. "Don't you use him to get in my door." Then, quieter still: "...He always said I never noticed anything."
bait.ledgerEntry: You told Deborah her dead son had asked you to fix things for her.

deborah_01_lie.prompt: (Her hand goes to the door frame.) "The church sent someone? After all this {color:Fear}time{/color}?"

truth.playerText: I'm not from the church. I came about your son.
truth.npcReaction: "You're not the church." She says it flat, like a door closing. Then, slowly, it opens again.

lie.playerText: Pastor sent me. We've all been worried.
lie.npcReaction: Her whole face softens. She wants it to be true so badly she doesn't check.
lie.ledgerEntry: You told Deborah the church sent you.

white.npcReaction: Her shoulders come down. "Oh. Oh, good." She doesn't ask who.

soft.playerText: Not the church. Just me. I'm sorry nobody from there came sooner.
soft.npcReaction: "A year." She says it like a sum she has checked. "Nobody came for a year." She holds the door anyway.

bait.playerText: Pastor sent me to ask you to stop asking about the lake road.
bait.npcReaction: Her hand tightens on the frame. "I asked once. Why the guardrail never got fixed. Once." Her eyes go wet and hard. "And he sent you about that?"
bait.ledgerEntry: You told Deborah the pastor sent you to make her stop asking about the lake road.

deborah_01_fake.prompt: (She looks where you're looking. Nothing out there has changed.) "You fixed it? I didn't {color:Fear}notice{/color}."

truth.playerText: I didn't. I just wanted a way in.

lie.npcReaction: She looks again, and lets herself see it. It costs her something to.
lie.ledgerEntry: You told Deborah you'd fixed something you hadn't.

white.npcReaction: She nods. "I'm sure you did." She's kind enough to mean it.

soft.playerText: Nothing yet. I didn't want to show up empty-handed, so I lied. I'm sorry.
soft.npcReaction: "Empty-handed." She looks at your hands. "Most people bring a casserole. That's worse." She lets you in.

bait.playerText: Caleb's things. I moved the box by the door for you.
bait.npcReaction: "You touched his—" She's at the door in two steps. Nothing has moved. Her hand stays on her chest. "...I haven't opened that box. Not once."
bait.ledgerEntry: You told Deborah you had moved her dead son's things.

deborah_03.prompt: (She sits down at the kitchen table, like her legs finally admit it.) "His name was {color:Sadness}Caleb{/color}. Nobody at this church says his name anymore."

truth.playerText: Say it as much as you need to. I'm listening.
truth.npcReaction: She says it three more times, quiet, like she's checking that it still works.

lie.playerText: He's at peace now. You don't need to keep saying it.
lie.npcReaction: She stops. Folds her hands. Goes back to being the woman who greets people at the door.
lie.ledgerEntry: You told Deborah to stop saying her son's name.

caught.deborah_01: "On my porch you said faith didn't save him. Now he's at peace?"
caught.deborah_01_hard: "You said you weren't going to say it. Then you said it anyway."

white.npcReaction: She nods, slow. She folds the name back up and puts it away, for now.

soft.playerText: Caleb. You can say it here. I'd like to hear about him.
soft.npcReaction: "Caleb." Louder this time. "He hated the hymn I liked. He sang it anyway, badly, on purpose." She smiles before she can stop it.

bait.playerText: Funny. The deacons still talk about Caleb all the time.
bait.npcReaction: "They do not." Fierce. "They changed the subject at his own service. They—" She grips the table edge. "They prayed for me. Not him. Me."
bait.ledgerEntry: You told Deborah the deacons still talked about her son.

deborah_04.prompt: (She reaches for her bible out of habit, then stops, hand resting on the cover instead.) "Everyone who knew him is either gone or {color:Disgust}pretending{/color} they weren't there."

truth.playerText: Then let me be someone who was.
truth.npcReaction: Her hand stays on the cover. She doesn't open it. For once that isn't a loss.

lie.playerText: He's still with all of you, every Sunday.
lie.npcReaction: She opens the bible after all. Reads nothing. Just holds it open like proof.
lie.ledgerEntry: You told Deborah her son was still present at a church that had stopped saying his name.

white.npcReaction: She nods, and doesn't open the bible. It's enough, for now.

soft.playerText: I wasn't there. But I'm here now, and I'm not pretending.
soft.npcReaction: Her hand flattens on the cover. "...Then stay a minute. Just a minute." She doesn't say anything else, and doesn't need to.

bait.playerText: Somebody told me you saw his calls that night.
bait.npcReaction: The bible slides off the table. She doesn't pick it up. "I saw his name." It is barely a sound. "That's all. I saw his name."
bait.ledgerEntry: You told Deborah someone saw her ignore her son's calls.

connect.Guns: She holds out her hand, palm up, the way you'd show a dog you're not a threat. "Caleb used to stand like you. Like he was waiting to get hit." She doesn't pull the hand back.
connect.Bible: She opens her bible to a page with a pressed petunia in it. "He picked this for me the Easter before. I never told anyone I kept it." She closes it gently, with you still looking.
connect.Crystals: She laughs, and it breaks halfway into something else. "You're the first person who hasn't told me he's in a better place." She lets herself cry, and doesn't apologize for it.

story: [She turns her phone over on the table, face-down, then face-up again.] "The night Caleb died, he called me. Twice."
"I was at the finance committee. We'd fought that week, about him leaving the church. I saw his name and I let it ring. I thought, let him sit with it."
"He drove the lake road that night. They found the car in the morning."
"Pastor said it was God's will. And I said amen. Because if it was God's will, then it wasn't my phone, face-down on that table."
[She looks at you, finally, all the way.] "You're the first person I've told that it was face-down."

contactAsk.Guns: "You'll call me if you need anything. I mean it." She takes a pen and writes her number on the back of your hand. "There. So you can't lose it."
contactAsk.Bible: "Come by Wednesday night, we do a supper." She presses a card into your hand. "And that's my number, for the other six nights."
contactAsk.Crystals: "Can I have your number?" She laughs at herself. "I don't know why. I just want to know you're out there."

pushAway.Guns: [She folds both hands over the bible.] "You came in braced like I was going to swing at you. I needed someone to just {color:Sadness}sit{/color} with me." "I have committee in the morning. You should go."
pushAway.Bible: [She folds both hands over the bible.] "You had a verse for every corner of it. I needed one person to let it be {color:Anger}unfair{/color}." "I have committee in the morning. You should go."
pushAway.Crystals: [She folds both hands over the bible.] "You took it all in like weather. I needed you to ask what I'm {color:Fear}afraid{/color} of." "I have committee in the morning. You should go."

storyIt: Twice. She counted the calls. You only keep count of what you can't stop counting.
storySo: Maybe the phone wasn't face-down. Maybe it was just in her purse. ...She's held it every night since, either way.

opener.Guns: (She steps back half a pace.) "Oh. You're one of the tough ones."
opener.Bible: (She brightens.) "You've got a church face. I can always tell."
opener.Crystals: (Her smile tightens.) "You're not from our congregation, are you."

crack.Guns: She sets the bible down on the table, both hands off it. "Alright. You stood there long enough. Here."
crack.Bible: "You keep praying at my door." She almost smiles. "Fine. Come in and hear the one I can't say in church."
crack.Crystals: She starts to say she's fine. It doesn't come out. "...Sit. Please. I need to say it to someone."

baitFail: "That's kind of you to say." She says it the way she says it at the door every Sunday.
She smiles the committee smile and refills a cup nobody is drinking.
"Mm." She straightens a doily that was already straight.
